DAL.head: The Stars should be in control
DAL.body: Even though Dallas may be without Heiskanen, the Stars have been out-chancing opponents by a wide margin lately and have home-ice advantage. On top of that, San Jose is on the second night of a back-to-back. It’s on the Sharks to make it a game, and they can if they keep shots to a minimum.

story.head: Rantanen’s favorite opponent
paras: The Stars won the teams’ first meeting this season, 5-0 in Dallas on Oct 5. The Stars (9-5-2) lost 2-1 in a shootout to Columbus on Thursday, and the Sharks are on a four-game losing streak. Going in, the Sharks are sixth in the Pacific (tied for 24th in the NHL) and the Stars third in the Central (tied for 11th).
This season, the Stars have outscored teams 44-36, but only 29-26 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 9-5, and no team creates more chances on the power play.

The Sharks do a lot of their shooting from distance (3rd lowest), are one of the league’s most physical teams (3rd) and ice the puck a lot (32nd). San Jose has scored 2.44 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. As for the Stars, they block more shots than anyone (1st) and play slow, tight games (lowest). They also have the league’s most dangerous power play (1st), and that could do real damage against the Sharks’ penalty kill (28th). Dallas has allowed 2.25 goals a game, the second fewest in the league. That means the Stars are likely to get in the way of a lot of the Sharks’ shots.

Macklin Celebrini (7 G / 11 A / 18 P in 16 GP) is carrying the Sharks’ offense. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (9 G / 10 A / 19 P in 16 GP) leads the way in scoring, with a point in eight straight games against San Jose. Jason Robertson (8 G / 10 A / 18 P in 16 GP) is next in line.
Yaroslav Askarov (4-8-0 / .885 SV% in 12 GS) is in line to start for San Jose. Jake Oettinger (8-3-1 / .910 SV% in 12 GS) has been outstanding for Dallas and will likely start.
The Stars usually control more of the chances than the Sharks do.
